body.en: Sketching standard curves and applying translations, reflections and stretches.
\( f(x)+a \) shifts up by \( a \); \( f(x-a) \) shifts right by \( a \); \( -f(x) \) reflects in the \( x \)-axis; \( af(x) \) stretches vertically by factor \( a \).

Domain Restrictions, Invertibility & Asymptotic Behavior: An algebraic or transcendental function \(f: D \to R\) possesses an inverse \(f^{-1}: R \to D\) if and only if \(f\) is strictly one-to-one (bijective) on \(D\), guaranteeing that \(\text{dom}(f^{-1}) = \text{ran}(f)\) and \(\text{ran}(f^{-1}) = \text{dom}(f)\). For logarithmic and radical equations, every algebraic step that squares both sides or combines logs (\(\log_b u + \log_b v = \log_b(uv)\)) can enlarge the solution set, requiring a final domain check against the original equation.

caption.en: Transformation of \(y = x^2\) to \(y = 2(x-2)^2 - 3\): translated by \(\begin{pmatrix}2\\-3\end{pmatrix}\) and stretched vertically by scale factor 2.

body.en:
Horizontal vs vertical operations: Operations inside the argument \(f(\dots)\) affect \(x\) inversely: \(f(x-a)\) translates right by \(+a\), and \(f(kx)\) stretches horizontally by scale factor \(\tfrac{1}{k}\). Operations outside affect \(y\) directly: \(af(x)\) stretches vertically by \(a\), and \(f(x)+c\) shifts up by \(c\).

Order of horizontal transformations: For \(f(ax+b)\), always factor the bracket: \(f\left(a(x + \tfrac{b}{a})\right)\). This represents a horizontal stretch by scale factor \(\tfrac{1}{a}\) followed by a translation by vector \(\begin{pmatrix}-\frac{b}{a}\\0\end{pmatrix}\), OR a translation of \(-b\) followed by stretch of \(\tfrac{1}{a}\). Stating transformations in the wrong order loses all marks.

Reflection axes: \(y = -f(x)\) is a reflection in the \(x\)-axis (\(y \to -y\)). \(y = f(-x)\) is a reflection in the \(y\)-axis (\(x \to -x\)).

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Graphs & Transformations)

body.en:
Why Completing the Square & Log-Linearization Work: Any quadratic \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) (\(a \ne 0\)) can be rewritten by factoring \(a\) from the first two terms and adding/subtracting \((b/2a)^2\):

\[ ax^2 + bx + c = a\!\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 + \left(c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\right) \]

Because \(\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 \ge 0\) for all \(x \in \mathbb{R}\), the extreme value \(k = c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\) is attained uniquely at the axis of symmetry \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), restricting the range to \([k, \infty)\) (if \(a > 0\)) and making \(f\) invertible on \(x \ge -\frac{b}{2a}\). Similarly, applying \(\ln\) to power laws \(y = ax^n\) yields \(\ln y = n\ln x + \ln a\), transforming a nonlinear curve into a straight line of gradient \(n\).

Describe \( y=(x-2)^{2} \) relative to \( y=x^{2} \).

It is a translation \( 2 \) units to the right.

Describe \( y=-x^{2} \) relative to \( y=x^{2} \).

A reflection in the \( x \)-axis.

Problem (Medium): A connected weighted graph \( E \) on vertices \( C, D, E, D \) has a minimum spanning tree with edge weights \( 7, 11, \) and \( 5 \). Find the total spanning tree weight \( W(E_{p}) \).

Step-by-Step Solution: Summing the tree edges gives \( 7 + 11 + 5 = 23 \).

Problem (Hard): In the plane, vertex \( C(1, 1) \) is translated by vector \( \mathbf{p} = \begin{pmatrix} 12 \\ 25 \end{pmatrix} \) to \( C'(13, 26) \). Find the coordinate sum \( E(C') \).

Step-by-Step Solution: The image point is \( (13, 26) \), with coordinate sum \( 13 + 26 = 39 \).

caption.en: Error Diagnosis — Common Student Traps vs. Exam-Board Method (Graphs & Transformations)

rows.en: Confuses the product law \(\ln(xy) = \ln x + \ln y\) with a non-existent sum rule.
Only factor products, quotients, and powers inside logarithms: \(\ln(xy) = \ln x + \ln y\).
Keeping both roots of \(\sqrt{2x+7} = x - 1\) without checking \(x - 1 \ge 0\)
Squaring both sides loses the sign of \(x - {r}\), introducing roots where \(\sqrt{\cdot} = -\text{number}\).
Enforce the range condition \(x \ge 1\) before or after squaring.
Restricting domain of \(f(x) = (x-3)^2 + 1\) to \(x \ge 0\) for invertibility
The vertex is at \(x = 3\), so \(f(2) = f(4) = 2\) fails the horizontal line test on \(x \ge 0\).
Restrict the domain at the vertex axis of symmetry: \(x \ge 3\) (or \(x \le 3\)).

label.en: ▲ Exam Pacing & Verification Strategy — Graphs & Transformations

body.en: Fast Exam Check (Cambridge International AS Level (9709 Paper 1 / Paper 4 / Paper 5)): To verify an inverse function \(f^{-1}(x)\) in 5 seconds, pick a simple input \(x_0\), compute \(y_0 = f(x_0)\), and check that \(f^{-1}(y_0) = x_0\). Also verify that the graph of \(y = f^{-1}(x)\) reflects \(y = f(x)\) across \(y = x\).

question.en: The curve \(y = f(x)\) has a stationary point at \((4, -6)\). State the coordinates of the corresponding stationary point on the curve: (a) \(y = f(x+3) + 2\), (b) \(y = 3f(2x)\), (c) \(y = -f(-x)\).

solution.en:
(a) \(y = f(x+3)+2\) translates 3 units left and 2 units up: \((4-3, -6+2) = (1, -4)\).
(b) \(y = 3f(2x)\) stretches horizontally by \(\tfrac{1}{2}\) and vertically by 3: \(\left(4 \times \tfrac{1}{2}, -6 \times 3\right) = (2, -18)\).
(c) \(y = -f(-x)\) reflects in both axes (point reflection through the origin): \((-4, -(-6)) = (-4, 6)\).

question.en: The curve \(y = x^2 - 6x + 5\) can be mapped to \(y = x^2\) by a sequence of two geometric transformations. Express the equation in vertex form, state the vertex, and describe fully each transformation.

solution.en: Complete the square: \(y = (x-3)^2 - 9 + 5 = (x-3)^2 - 4\). The vertex of the parabola is \((3, -4)\). To map \(y = (x-3)^2 - 4\) back to \(y = x^2\), we must translate the graph 3 units to the left and 4 units upwards. In vector notation, this is a single translation by \(\begin{pmatrix}-3\\4\end{pmatrix}\), or two sequential transformations: (1) Translation by vector \(\begin{pmatrix}-3\\0\end{pmatrix}\) (3 units left), and (2) Translation by vector \(\begin{pmatrix}0\\4\end{pmatrix}\) (4 units up).
